zh.title: 空中巴士與法國航空成立合資公司 專注A350航材與維修支援
zh.summary: 空中巴士與法國航空成立合資企業；管理全球A350航材共享庫；已支援逾500架飛機。
body: 空中巴士（Airbus）與法國航空（Air France）於2026年10月28日完成設立持股各半的合資企業「Alpha Component Solutions」，專門為空中巴士A350客機營運商提供零組件支援。該新實體將由空中巴士與荷蘭皇家航空集團（Air France-KLM）共同營運，管理全球共享航材庫，提供機隊零組件資產、維護服務、供應鏈管理以及修理作業。
該合資企業整合了空中巴士的 Flight Hours Services（FHS）與法國航空－荷蘭皇家航空工程與維護部門（AFI KLM E&M）的資源。目前該企業已依合約支援超過500架飛機。根據 AeroTime 報導，首架 A350 於2015年在卡達航空投入服務，空中巴士截至目前已交付737架 A350 機型，並手握 1,624 架待交付訂單。

en.title: Airbus and Air France Finalise Joint Venture Alpha Component Solutions for A350 Support
en.summary: Airbus and Air France launch Alpha Component Solutions; manages worldwide A350 component pool; supports over 500 aircraft.
body: Airbus and Air France have finalized the establishment of a 50-50 joint venture named Alpha Component Solutions, dedicated to supporting Airbus A350 operators worldwide. The new entity is operated jointly between Airbus and Air France-KLM to manage a global shared-access pool, providing aircraft component assets, maintenance services, supply chain management, and repair capabilities for A350 customers.

By combining the capabilities of Airbus Flight Hours Services (FHS) and Air France Industries KLM Engineering & Maintenance (AFI KLM E&M), the joint venture contractually supports more than 500 aircraft. According to AeroTime, the first A350 entered service in 2015 with Qatar Airways, and Airbus has delivered 737 A350 aircraft to date alongside orders for 1,624 more.

zh.title: 印度新創Nalwa Aero完成箱型翼電動垂直起降機試飛
zh.summary: Nalwa Aero；完成箱型翼eVTOL縮比機試飛；驗證懸停與前飛性能
body: 印度新創公司Nalwa Aero已成功完成其縮比箱型翼電動垂直起降（eVTOL）航空器的飛行測試。本次初步試飛採用電力推進系統與全傾轉旋翼系統，成功驗證了該機型的懸停與向前飛行能力。
這家總部位於印度北部旁遮普邦的新創企業表示，未來計畫將此非傳統翼型架構發展為五座平臺，用於載客運輸、空中救護車與貨運業務。印度民航部長奈杜在會見公司創辦人桑德胡與技術長薩拉斯後，對這項技術進展表示歡迎。

en.title: Indian Startup Nalwa Aero Conducts Flight Tests of Box-Wing eVTOL Aircraft
en.summary: Nalwa Aero flight-tests scaled box-wing eVTOL aircraft in India; demonstrates hovering and forward flight
body: Indian startup Nalwa Aero has successfully completed flight tests of its scaled box-wing electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. The preliminary flight trials demonstrated hovering and forward flight using electric propulsion and an all-tilting-rotor system, marking an early milestone for the technology.

Based in the northern state of Punjab, Nalwa Aero plans to develop the concept into a five-seat platform targeted at passenger transport, air ambulances, and cargo operations. Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu welcomed the progress after meeting founder Kuljeet Singh Sandhu and chief technology officer Nelson Salas.

India’s Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu welcomed the development after meeting Sandhu and Nalwa Aero chief technology officer Nelson Salas, who briefed him on the company’s progress.

The company, based in India’s northern state of Punjab, said the preliminary trials demonstrated that its unusual wing arrangement could support both vertical and forward flight, an important early step towards developing a full-sized aircraft.
